Brand: Rosmonde

## Features
Perfect for 5 Subjects: This spiral notebook is great for keeping organized and taking notes in up to 5 classes or projects; 6 Pack: This 5 subject notebook is all you need! No more worrying about keeping track of multiple notebooks; Keep Organized: With 150 wide ruled, double sided sheets, there is plenty of room to take well organized notes; Durable Design: Spiral bindings are created to keep your notes together by being resistant to uncoiling and snagging on objects; 3-Hole Punched: Every notebook comes 3-hole punched to fit a standard binder; take along one notebook or several to save extra trips to the locker

## Pricing & Reviews
Price: 27.99 USD.
Rated 4.3 from 64 reviews.
Top review: Paper is super thin and pencil smudges really easilyWide ruled paper is NOT the size of choice for College! Hole punches in paper do not line up to put in binder.The notebooks came unbent and packaged together with protective plastic. They are standard size in assorted colors. The spiral bound, non perforated pages turn well. The pages are crisp and white. Pretty typical notebook. The covers aren't horrible (nothing special either) but they aren't really any more or less durable then any other common notebook you'd buy.I honestly do not understand why "reviewers" do not review and that many that do, miss the boat, entirely.SPECIFICATIONSPages: 10.44” x 7.81” (26.52 cm x 19.84 cm; unperforated; NOT recycled;NOTE: Includes 1.16” (2.95 cm) top margin; 1.19” (3.02 cm) left margin:Wide (college) ruled spacing: 0.34” (0.87 cm):Notebook thickness: 0.25” (0.64 cm):Weight: 8.38 oz (0.24 kg):Spiral wire diameter: 0.044” (1.12mm);Spiral wire spacing: 0.29” (7.3 mm)Number of spiral-wire holes: 33NOTE: my “back to school sale” (as one reviewer categorized them) spiral notebook has a spiral wire diameter of 0.038” (0.97 mm) and a spiral wire spacing of 0.22” (5.6 mm). In other words, the spiral wire on this Rosemond notebook is 15% thicker than the “school sale” notebook and its spacing is 23% greater. The number of spiral-wire holes in the Rosemond notebook is 33; the school-sale notebook has 42: 21% more. The spiral-wire hole size is the same for either notebook. The significance of these data follows.Colors I received: blue, yellow, red, dark pink (light purple)USESFor me, one-subject notebooks facilitate collecting and filing data by category, time (e.g., yearly), individual (e.g., staff), project, etc.SUBJECTIVEWith spiral notebooks, I prefer one subject. In my hands, with regular use, spiral notebooks eventually fail as their pages rip free from the spiral wire with repeated access. This eventuality is hastened with multisubject notebooks that, of necessity, require more frequent access in proportion to the number of subjects. If my needs exceed the one subject, 70-page capacity, notebook, I prefer multiple notebooks per subject (e.g., part 1, part 2, etc.) instead of one, high-capacity multisubject notebook.So, what about these Rosemond notebooks. To me, there are two outstanding features: a heavier gauge spiral wire and spiral-wire perforations that are more widely spaced apart than the aforementioned school-sale notebooks. Think about it: the heavier gauge spiral wire is stiffer and not going to flex; there is less added pressure on the holes as the notebook is used. The heavier gauge spiral wire is thicker than its thinner cousin and, as a result, is less apt to saw its way through the paper. (A thin wire will “saw” its way through the paper easier than a thicker wire.) The hole sizes in the two notebooks are the same but the Rosemond has 21% fewer holes spread across the page. As a result, there is more paper between the holes. i.e., the tags of paper between the holes are larger and more tear- or saw-resistant.Without a detailed explanation, Rosemond identifies its “durable design” on the product page, which I suggest is due to the characteristics I have identified – characteristics that have eluded reviewers – and characteristics that, to me, justify the modest cost increase compared with inferior products.Finally, I am impelled to comment on one reviewer who characterized (and degraded) these notebooks as “extremely simple without even perforated edges at the spiraling and an ugly design on the front.” Maybe it says a lot about me, but I do not buy notebooks based on their beauty. To each their own but it surprises me how many people judge books/people by their cover and, as in the case of this notebook, completely miss its superior utilitarian purpose and design. What does “without even perforated edges at the spiraling” mean? One can only guess because the holes are machine-punched and are same size and in the same location on the paper. When open, the left and right pages and holes are offset BY DESIGN! as they follow the path of the spiral wire. (When the notebook is closed, the holes line up perfectly. Duh . . .. But even at that, if the notebook opens without binding and lays flat on the table or desk, who cares what the alignment of the holes is on opposing pages – and why do they care?I find these Rosemond 70-page, one-subject spiral notebooks to be well made and sturdier than most due to their heavy-gauge-wire construction. Are they a better value than their cheaper cousins, of course. Will they last longer, i.e., will the pages not as readily rip from the spiral wire, time will tell but they give every indication of superior strength compared to their school-sale alternatives. I highly recommend them.Sturdy and great notebooksThese are your standard generic notebooks. Same quality and everything as what you would find at the grocery store.These spirals are fine for wide ruled single subject notebooks but they are way overpriced. I would expect these to be no more than about $2 each, and maybe half of that in the back to school sale. They are extremely simple without even perforated edges at the spiraling and an ugly design on the front. The paper is ordinary and marked with deep blue lines and pink 1 inch margins. These are totally fine except that at $4 each, they are way overpriced.$4 each is like a premium price, but this is definitely not a set of premium notebooks.

# Mead Spiral Notebook, 5 Subject, College Ruled Paper, 180 Sheets, 10-1/2" x 8", Color Selected For You, 1 Count (05682)
Brand: Mead
Category: Notebooks & Writing Pads > Spiral Notebooks

## Features
5 subject spiral notebook gives you the ability to manage notes for up to 5 classes or projects in one place. Notebook covers are coated for durability.; White paper; 180 sheets, 10.5 in. x 8 in. page size. Assorted cover colors - color selected may vary. Pages are college ruled and double-sided to provide plenty of notetaking space.; Notebook spiral binding will not snag and resists uncoiling to keep your notes together. Handy dividers separate the notebook into 5 different subjects.

## Pricing & Reviews
Price: 9.96 USD.
Rated 4.6 from 134 reviews.
Top review: I ordered a white notebook because it was the cheapest but got a red one which is fine with me. Of course, if someone really needed a white notebook, that would be an issue. This is your run of the mill 5 subject notebook. It is college ruled and a little smaller than others but not by much. The cover is a cardboard and it feels a little cheap all around but it suffice. I just want this notebook to use as a sort of journal so I won't be hauling it around. I do think it may get tattered quickly if it is put into a book bag and removed a lot. A plastic cover would hold up much better.There are no tabs indicating each subject, just a plain tan sheet. Again, for me, that's great. It does have perforations to remove the pages without the mess of spiral bound shards and it does have holes in the page on the side for placing in binders. If you need something sturdy and more collegiate, this one is not for you. As a simple, inexpensive notebook, it's fine.I don’t know why the picture shows three notebooks when you’re only getting one but I guess it’s because of the color that you can choose but either way you can just select the color and then a picture should appear about what color you choose It’s crazy confusing but I got a notebook and I hope is good…. for writing but other than that it’s pretty small compared to this one that my mom or my sister got from Staples and the front page it’s just box and the last page is also box and more lighter than the one in the front both five subjects but different stores and different price but this one was way cheaper but the thing is that it’s more it’s small and the lines are super faded compared to the one from StaplesI like the notebookWhat I don't like is the lines.They are not dark enoughAwesome paper!I bought this for my son for school and can't believe it came in a huge box with way too much packaging. It was specified for school supplies and I was looking for a better product, it needed that packaging because it was very flimsy. Oh well, live and learn. I was more disappointed in myself for creating so much waste.Exactly as described, good value, all in tact and no issuesIt's a pretty standard five subject notebook. The paper feels really thin though. Pen marks may easily go through the paper when writing so keep that in mind.Serves its purposeLa mejor que encontré entre las opciones para trabajos de mi hija en la escuela (primaria), excelente precio-calidad-cantidad y grosor de hojas.
